## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Port of Acurast `apps/app-cargo-python`, and the representative draft for the
## whole eleven-example language matrix.
##
## Its application logic is trivial on purpose. Everything interesting is the
## runtime contract: findings #1 (image selection), #2 (dependency install),
## #3 (what "the process" is), #13 (the script is the wrong layer).

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: cargo-python

metadata:
  description: Run a Python program under the Cargo/PRoot runtime.
  labels: [liskov, example, cargo, language-matrix, python]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: native_image

  # PROPOSED — finding #1. Upstream pins a Termux proot-distro tarball URL and
  # sha256; Liskov will not accept that (ADR-0041 owns the supply chain), but
  # V4's raw `imageDigest` makes every manifest hard-code a digest that rots on
  # each image revision. A catalogue name plus a version floor, resolved to an
  # exact digest at publication, is what this schema proposes.
  image:
    name: debian-trixie
    version: "0.1"

  entrypoint:
    # V5 carries no multi-line shell body. The script is a repository file built
    # into the image and invoked explicitly; no consumer reparses a command
    # string. Under finding #13 this whole file should eventually disappear
    # into a declared install phase.
    executable: /bin/sh
    args: ["/app/start.sh"]

execution:
  mode: once

deployment:
  schedule:
    duration: 10m
  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "200000"

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Port of Acurast `apps/app-cargo-ssh`: an interactive shell into a processor.
##
## Earlier revisions of this draft deliberately kept `acurast_tunnel` after
## ADR-0059 §6, because it was the one port whose purpose was to show SSH riding
## the tunnel. ADR-0082 §3.d defers every SSH provider except `liskov_managed`
## out of V5, so that demonstration has no schema left to stand on and this
## draft follows the mapping rule the rest of the catalogue already used. What
## it shows now is the mandatory §2.f arm on its own: authenticated operator
## access with no ingress beside it, costing zero tunnel connections, so
## ownership of the two-connection budget is unambiguous by construction rather
## than by argument.
##
## The tunnel-backed variant is future-version evidence; see
## `applications/README.md`.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: cargo-ssh

metadata:
  description: Open an interactive shell into a processor over authenticated Runtime SSH.
  labels: [liskov, example, cargo, access, ssh]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: native_image
  image: # PROPOSED — finding #1
    name: debian-trixie
    version: "0.1"
  entrypoint:
    executable: /bin/sh
    args: ["/app/start.sh"]
execution:
  mode: continuous

deployment:
  schedule:
    duration: 1h
  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "600000"
    rate:
      amount: "15000000"
      window: 1d

access:
  # ADR-0045: authenticated operator access is NOT public ingress. V5 moves
  # Runtime SSH out of V4's `ingress.ssh` into its own section. Absence means
  # disabled — there is no `mode`, no `optional` arm, and no redundant disabled
  # object.
  ssh:
    provider:
      kind: liskov_managed

  # Upstream also offers ngrok and pinggy arms selected by SSH_TUNNEL. Those
  # are deliberately NOT ported: a user-supplied third-party tunnel token has
  # no integration record, no audit trail, and no revocation path.

configuration:
  secrets:
    - secretId: cargo-ssh-password
      required: true
      destination:
        kind: environment
        name: SSH_PASSWORD

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Port of Acurast `apps/app-env-vars`. The V5 configuration surface: a closed
## literal-vs-managed source union with no `managed` boolean, and secrets with
## explicit destinations.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: env-vars

metadata:
  description: Read literal configuration, an application-managed value, and a secret.
  labels: [liskov, example, javascript, configuration]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: javascript
  engine: nodejs
  entrypoint:
    file: bundle.js
execution:
  # Upstream is `interval`. Blocked on BKLG-20260730-e627, which waits for the
  # complete V5 occurrence contract rather than creating a second schedule
  # authority.
  mode: interval
  every: 1h

deployment:
  schedule:
    duration: 30s
  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "20000"
    # REQUIRED because execution is recurring (Q-20260810-v2xn). A per-job cap
    # alone bounds one occurrence; an `interval` application runs forever, and
    # the org guard is not a fallback — `SpendGuards.budget_cap` defaults to
    # `None`, meaning no cap.
    rate:
      amount: "500000"
      window: 30d

configuration:
  variables:
    # Literal: authored, digested, visible, immutable without republishing.
    - name: GREETING
      source: literal
      value: hello
    # Application-managed: the policy declares the name and requiredness; the
    # value lives in the Application's value store and changes without a new
    # policy version. `default` is valid only on this arm — it is the fallback
    # for a mutable out-of-policy value, not a digested constant.
    #
    # Note what is ABSENT: `delivery`. In V4 this is where finding #7 bites —
    # only the `slipway` arm resolves and the unresolved `acurast` arm is the
    # default. This schema's answer is to remove the choice from authoring
    # entirely and let the platform pick the mechanism.
    - name: REPORT_LABEL
      source: managed
      required: false
      default: nightly
  secrets:
    # Rides the ADR-0014 Lockbox path, which is complete and in production.
    - secretId: my-secret-env-var
      required: true
      destination:
        kind: environment
        name: MY_SECRET_ENV_VAR

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## Port of Acurast `apps/app-fetch`: GET data from one API, POST it to another.

## measured against — one JavaScript job, once, no ingress, no state.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: fetch

metadata:
  description: Fetch data from an API and post it to another API.
  labels: [liskov, example, javascript, batch]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: javascript
  engine: nodejs
  entrypoint:
    # Relative to the immutable artifact root (`dist/`), which the trusted
    # source integration owns — not relative to the repository.
    file: bundle.js
execution:
  mode: once

deployment:
  schedule:
    # Upstream: maxExecutionTimeInMs 30000. No startAt / maxAllowedStartDelay —
    # the platform's `standard` launch-timing profile owns both.
    duration: 30s
  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "50000"

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Port of Acurast `apps/app-puppeteer`: scrape the web from many processors at
## once. Upstream runs 64 replicas; this is the catalogue's real test of V5 job
## count and phasing.
##
## Upstream's other reason for running on Acurast is source diversity, which
## earlier revisions expressed as `placement.spread` on `wan_ip` and `country`.
## ADR-0082 §3.e defers the whole diversity vocabulary out of V5, and the
## production capability surface has never had `topology_constraints` enabled,
## so that block promised something no author could obtain. Following the
## porting rule, this states the substitution rather than reproducing it: the
## port keeps the parallelism and drops the diversity claim. Restoring it is
## future-version work; see `applications/README.md`.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: puppeteer

metadata:
  description: Scrape the web with Puppeteer from many independent processors.
  labels: [liskov, example, javascript, batch, parallel]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: javascript
  engine: nodejs
  entrypoint:
    file: bundle.js
execution:
  mode: once

deployment:
  # Upstream numberOfReplicas: 64. Total desired simultaneous job capacity —
  # Liskov derives slot identity, membership, and offsets. The author never
  # names a slot.
  jobs: 64

  schedule:
    duration: 1m
    phasing:
      # All 64 at once: this is a scrape, not a rolling service. Stated
      # explicitly because the same field is what shard-worker sets to
      # evenly_spaced, where it becomes the rolling-renewal mechanism.
      mode: simultaneous

  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "100000"

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Reference application, not an Acurast catalogue port. It exists because the
## catalogue expresses rolling renewal only through clustered database services
## (cockroachdb-ha, postgres, rqlite), and every one of those also needs public
## ingress and durable state. That coupling made `evenly_spaced` phasing look
## like a property of stateful clusters, when it is really a property of any
## multi-job deployment that must not retire its whole fleet at one instant.
##
## A sharded queue worker is the smallest honest carrier: three jobs, each
## pulling its own shard of an external work queue, reaching nothing inbound.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: shard-worker

metadata:
  description: Drain a partitioned work queue from three independently renewing jobs.
  labels: [liskov, reference, javascript, batch, parallel]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: javascript
  engine: nodejs
  entrypoint:
    file: bundle.js
execution:
  mode: continuous

deployment:
  # Three shards. Liskov derives slot identity and membership; the worker reads
  # its shard index from the platform-supplied job metadata, never from policy.
  jobs: 3

  schedule:
    duration: 6h
    phasing:
      # One job per phase across a six-hour window staggers renewal by two
      # hours, so exactly one shard is ever at its boundary. `simultaneous`
      # would retire all three together, on a schedule.
      mode: evenly_spaced
      jobsPerPhase: 1

  lifecycle:
    update:
      existingJobs:
        # A shard is an exclusive lease on a queue partition: two jobs must
        # never hold the same one. The predecessor serves out its paid window
        # and accepts the gap rather than overlapping with its successor.
        mode: run_until_scheduled_end

  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "3600000"
    rate:
      amount: "45000000"
      window: 1d

configuration:
  secrets:
    - secretId: shard-worker-queue-token
      required: true
      destination:
        kind: environment
        name: QUEUE_TOKEN

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

## DRAFT — validates against the proposed V5 schema. Not publishable.
##
## Reference application, not an Acurast catalogue port. It exists because the
## catalogue authors `placement.minimums` and file-destination secrets only on
## services that also publish ingress (clickhouse, cargo-hermes, wordpress) or
## keep durable state. Neither field has anything to do with either: a batch job
## can need a large device and a credentials file while reaching nothing inbound
## and keeping nothing across renewals.
##
## Transcoding is the clearest carrier — the work is CPU- and storage-bound, the
## input and output live in object storage, and the credentials for that store
## are a file because the SDK that reads them wants a path, not an environment
## variable.

schema: proof.liskov.application-manifest

schemaVersion: 5

applicationId: video-transcode

metadata:
  description: Transcode a queued video on a large processor and upload the result.
  labels: [liskov, reference, cargo, batch, media]

release:
  mode: source

runtime:
  kind: native_image
  image: # PROPOSED — finding #1
    name: debian-trixie
    version: "0.1"
  entrypoint:
    executable: /bin/sh
    args: ["/app/transcode.sh"]
execution:
  mode: once

deployment:
  schedule:
    duration: 30m

  placement:
    minimums:
      # Enforced on-chain via RequiredMinMetrics, fail-closed. Liskov adds 1.1x
      # selection headroom on top, so the effective floor is higher. `memory` is
      # TOTAL device RAM; `storage` is AVAILABLE space, and a 4K source plus its
      # intermediate frames is the reason this one is large.
      memory: 4GiB
      storage: 32GiB

  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
    perJob: "1800000"

configuration:
  variables:
    - source: literal
      name: TRANSCODE_PRESET
      value: h264-1080p

  secrets:
    - secretId: video-transcode-object-store-credentials
      required: true
      destination:
        # A file, not an environment variable: the object-store SDK this image
        # ships reads a credentials path. The file destination never collides
        # with a variable name, which is why it needs no collision rule.
        kind: file
        path: /etc/liskov/object-store-credentials.json
    - secretId: video-transcode-callback-token
      required: true
      destination:
        kind: environment
        name: CALLBACK_TOKEN

state:
  mode: off

observability:
  logs:
    enabled: true

# EXPECT: duplicate key
# EXPECT-CODE: invalid_manifest
# EXPECT-POINTER: /
#
# YAML permits duplicate mapping keys and most loaders silently keep the LAST.
# In a manifest that means one of two blocks quietly wins, and the discarded one
# leaves no trace: no error, no warning, nothing downstream can see it.
#
# This is not hypothetical. `meilisearch` carried two `placement` blocks and the
# reference validator reported `ok` for weeks -- PyYAML kept the second, so the
# first block's `spread` rules (wan_ip and operator diversity, on a three-job
# search cluster) were discarded at load time and never reached the schema.
# Found 2026-08-12 by the Rust port, whose loader rejects duplicates by
# construction.
#
# The rule is enforced at INGESTION, not by a schema keyword, because by the
# time a document is a dict the duplicate is already gone.

  mode: source

  kind: javascript

  spend:

    perJob: "1000000"

  spend:
    unit: service_credit_micros
